_readme: GEO feature taxonomy - the spine of the Tab 2 scorecard
(docs/ai/recommendation-two-tab-plan.md). Each feature is scored
identically against the QC page and the top cited pages for a topic.
detection: 'deterministic' = parsed from HTML by page_facts.py;
'semantic' = judged by the scorecard's LLM pass over the extracted text;
'ratio' = a numeric value computed by page_facts.py (or scorecard.py for
query_term_coverage) and scored against a fixed target_min/target_max
(unit: 'pct' or 'levels') from published GEO structural-citation research -
an ABSOLUTE literature target, not a winner-relative comparison. Ratio
features skip the winners_present/prevalence machinery entirely and surface
on the scorecard as `metric_rows`, not `features`.
geo_weight is a VETO FLOOR, not a ranker: prevalence among cited pages
ranks, weight only stops recommending high-prevalence-but-worthless
features. Features with weight 'low' are never auto-recommended.
confidence reflects how replicated/consistent the underlying research is
('high' = consistent across multiple independent studies, 'medium' = strong
but narrower/less-replicated findings, 'low' = single-study or contested) -
independent of geo_weight, so recommendation prose can be honest about
how much to trust a given signal.
Recommend rule (deterministic/semantic): prevalence high AND QC missing AND
geo_weight > low. Recommend rule (ratio): QC's measured value falls outside
[target_min, target_max].

features.label: Direct answer near top
features.description: Answers the topic's core question within the first ~150 words, before any product pitch. Judged against the topic's representative question.

features.label: Certification / pathway section
features.description: Explains certification requirements, professional bodies, and the path into the career - not just the course being sold.

features.label: Career outcomes / salary
features.description: Concrete outcomes: salary ranges, job titles, employment prospects, alumni results.

features.label: FAQ section
features.description: A visible Q&A section answering common questions in plain language.

features.label: FAQPage structured data
features.description: FAQPage JSON-LD present in the page source. Schema markup measures as near-zero independent effect once other structural/content factors are controlled for - treat as hygiene, not a primary lever.

features.label: Question-style headings
features.description: H2/H3s phrased as the questions people ask (how/what/can/should... or ending in '?'). Counted; >=2 counts as present.

features.label: Tuition / cost breakdown
features.description: Actual costs stated - tuition, fees, payment plans - not 'contact us for pricing'. Deterministic pricing_signals flag is a hint, the semantic pass confirms.

features.label: Comparison table
features.description: At least one HTML table comparing options/features/costs.

features.label: Named author / expert byline
features.description: A named author with stated credentials or first-hand experience (E-E-A-T signal).

features.label: Cites primary sources / professional bodies
features.description: References professional associations, government statistics, or original data rather than only self-referential claims.

features.label: Evidence density (stats, quotes, sources)
features.description: Concrete evidence woven through the text: statistics with numbers, quotations, or named sources - not just unsupported claims. A strong citation booster in most studies, but use judiciously: at least one benchmark (C-SEO Bench) found added statistics hurt citation ranking in 19/24 settings, so don't over-rely on stat-stuffing alone.

features.label: Neutral, third-person tone
features.description: Reads like reference material: no first-person blog voice, no hard sell. First-person/blog tone is the single strongest NEGATIVE predictor of citation across studies - marketing tone reduces the odds an engine quotes the page as an authority.

features.label: Comprehensive topic coverage
features.description: Fully answers the topic's question end-to-end (requirements, process, costs, outcomes) rather than covering one slice. Judged against the topic's representative question.

features.label: Extractable value propositions
features.description: Short, quotable justification claims an engine can lift when shortlisting ('A+ BBB rating', '21-day money-back guarantee') - stated plainly, not buried in prose.

features.label: Pros / cons section
features.description: An explicit pros-and-cons or advantages/drawbacks breakdown of the options discussed.

features.label: Comparison framing (X vs Y)
features.description: Side-by-side comparison of alternatives in the body text ('X vs Y', option-by-option contrasts) - beyond just having an HTML table, which comparison_table already detects. The strongest page-level citation predictor found, and it works across all query-intent types.

features.label: Organization/Course schema
features.description: Organization or Course JSON-LD present. Low weight: rarely distinguishes cited pages, and schema markup generally shows near-zero independent effect on citation.

features.label: Embedded video
features.description: Embedded YouTube/Vimeo/native video. Low weight: engagement signal, weak citation signal.

features.label: Internal linking density
features.description: Internal links as a share of all links in the main content (internal_links / total_links). Part of macro-structure, the largest single contributor (44.9%) to structural-optimization citation gains in the underlying study.
features.fix_below: Add more internal links to related QC pages within the body content - not just the nav/footer.
features.fix_above: Internal links dominate the page's total links - add a few outbound links to back up specific claims (a professional/certifying body, a government labor-statistics page for salary/demand figures, an industry report), or cut back on internal cross-links, so internal links aren't nearly all of them.

features.label: Heading hierarchy depth
features.description: Number of distinct heading levels (h1-h5) actually used in the main content. Macro-structure signal - deep, well-nested hierarchy mirrors how engines decompose a page into citable facts.
features.fix_below: Break long sections into nested subheadings (e.g. add H3s under each H2) instead of one flat run of H2s.
features.fix_above: The heading structure is unusually deep - flatten some nesting so the hierarchy still reads as a clear outline.

features.label: Structured content share
features.description: Share of main-content word count sitting inside lists, tables, or blockquote/comparison blocks. Meso-structure, the second-largest contributor (39.7%) to structural-optimization citation gains - distinct from comparison_table, which only checks whether at least one table exists at all.
features.fix_below: Convert more of the prose into bulleted/numbered lists, a comparison table, or a blockquote summary.
features.fix_above: Too much of the page is lists/tables - fold some of that back into explanatory paragraphs so key points aren't just fragments.

features.label: Paragraph length conformance
features.description: Share of paragraphs in the main content whose length falls in the 150-300 word sweet spot. Meso-structure signal - too-short paragraphs read as thin, too-long paragraphs bury the answer.
features.fix_below: Rewrite paragraphs to land in the 150-300 word range - merge choppy one-line paragraphs, split long ones that bury the point.

features.label: Bold/italic emphasis density
features.description: Share of main-content word count wrapped in bold/italic emphasis. Micro-structure - the smallest contributor (15.4%) to structural-optimization citation gains, so treat as a minor supporting signal, not a primary lever. (Emphasis weighted toward sentence beginnings is a further nuance this deterministic check does not model.)
features.fix_below: Bold or italicize key terms, numbers, and takeaways so a scanning reader (or engine) can find the answer fast.
features.fix_above: Bold/italic is overused - reserve it for the few phrases that actually need to stand out, or it stops meaning anything.

features.label: Query-term coverage
features.description: Share of the tracked question's significant (non-stopword) terms that appear verbatim in the page text. The page must contain the words people actually search - a page can be well-structured and still never surface if it doesn't use the query's own vocabulary. The 70% threshold is a working default, not a number from the underlying research.
features.fix_below: Work the question's own key words into the page's headings and body text directly, not just synonyms or paraphrases.
